- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged 3–5 day average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect risk-off → risk-on reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of 0.8–1.2% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits high variance; use 3-day moving average to smooth out erratic forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows recent downward trend, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
